:::{#sol-linear-map-practice}

Yes.
For any $\vx, \vy \in \reals^2$,
$f$ is [additive](#def-additive-function):

$$
\ba
f(\vx + \vy)
&= 3 (x_1 + y_1) - (x_2 + y_2)
&& \text{(@def-vector-addition)}
\\&= (3 x_1 - x_2) + (3 y_1 - y_2)
&& \text{(rearranging the terms)}
\\&= f(\vx) + f(\vy).
\ea
$$

For any $\vx \in \reals^2$ and $c \in \reals$,
$f$ is [homogeneous](#def-homogeneous-function):

$$
\ba
f(c \vx)
&= 3 c x_1 - c x_2
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult)}
\\&= c (3 x_1 - x_2)
&& \text{(factoring out } c \text{)}
\\&= c f(\vx).
\ea
$$

Since $f$ is both,
it is a [linear map](#def-linear-map).

:::
